clue.text: Least noble, as eclipsed by most noble

indicators.note: something eclipsed is hidden behind something larger, so the word as sits within the other piece

parts.note: the best are the most noble, the finest of all

explanation.surface: A comparison of rank in which the lowest of the aristocracy are overshadowed by the grandest.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means morally low or ignoble, so its superlative describes whoever has the least nobility.

clue.text: Open-air vocal music giving child good time at first

indicators.note: the time piece is placed at the front, before the child and good pieces

parts.note: bird is slang for a prison sentence, from 'birdlime', rhyming slang for time
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A child enjoying a sing-along outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdsong is the singing of wild birds, music performed outdoors by voice.

clue.text: American politician contributing to tense NATO row

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters that each of these words contributes, running across them

parts.note: the answer runs across these words: tenSE NATO Row

explanation.surface: A US lawmaker adds to a strained dispute within the military alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of the US Senate, the upper house of Congress.

clue.text: Thus a religious leader and artist combined for TV serial

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
the Pope leads the Roman Catholic Church
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A pontiff teams up with a painter to make a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running television drama series about ongoing domestic lives.

clue.text: Statistical diagram in Chapter I in error

indicators.note: letters in error are wrongly placed, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A book's first chapter contains a mistaken chart of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie chart is a circular graph showing proportions as slices, a common way of presenting statistics.

clue.text: Organised oral inspection, like teacher for pupils

indicators.note: the letters are put into a new order, organised into the answer phrase

explanation.surface: A school inspector holds a planned spoken examination of the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in place of a parent, the legal responsibility a teacher holds over children in school.

clue.text: Move quickly in sea, slowly on land

definitions.meaning: first meaning: swim the front ..., the fastest stroke
second meaning: creep along on hands and knees

explanation.walkthrough: The same word names the fastest swimming stroke and the slowest way of getting about on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The front crawl is a fast swimming stroke, while crawling on land is proverbially slow progress.

clue.text: Ungodly type present as robbery happens

parts.note: being at an event means being present there
a heist is a robbery, especially a daring one

explanation.surface: An irreligious man is on the scene when a raid takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist is someone who does not believe in any deity.

clue.text: One use of carbon, until now

definitions.meaning: first meaning: carbon dating is used to work out how old something is
second meaning: so far, up to the present

explanation.walkthrough: Radiocarbon dating measures decay of carbon-14 to estimate the age of organic remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes establishing the age of an object, and as an adverb it means up to the present moment.

clue.text: In respect of its being transformed, they demand the best

indicators.note: transformed letters change their arrangement, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fussy people insist on top quality, especially where change is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfectionists refuse to accept any standard short of flawless.

clue.text: Sounded alarm, perhaps, and initiated recall

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally struck a bell, as when raising an alarm
second meaning: the idiom for something seeming familiar and stirring a memory

explanation.surface: Someone raised the alarm and also triggered a product recall.
explanation.walkthrough: Recall reads like a withdrawal of faulty goods, but it means remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal act of striking a bell and an idiom for prompting someone to remember.

clue.text: Help introducing gardener's scientific measure for pest

indicators.note: the help word takes in another piece, which is introduced into its middle

parts.note: aid means help
pH is the scientific scale of acidity a gardener uses to test soil

explanation.surface: A gardener gets help by testing the soil scientifically to deal with a garden pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids such as greenfly are sap-sucking insects that damage garden plants, so gardeners treat them as a pest.

clue.text: Starts journey with radios out of operation

parts.note: radio sets: sets are receivers
a switched-off machine is not working

explanation.surface: A traveller begins a trip with the radios switched off.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is the phrasal verb for departing or beginning a trip.

clue.text: Musician has a life after bit of gaol time

indicators.note: the life piece comes after the gaol piece in the answer, so this word orders them

parts.note: a cell is one small part of a gaol (a British spelling of jail)
is in the sense of exists, to be alive

explanation.surface: A musician makes a fresh start in life after serving a spell in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Is here means exists, as in 'I think, therefore I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist is a player of the cello, the large bowed string instrument.

clue.text: Shark in harbour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... shark, a slow bottom-dwelling species
second meaning: to ... a grudge is to harbour it

explanation.walkthrough: In reads like a location for a shark in port, but it is just a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurse names a kind of shark and is also a verb meaning to cherish or keep a feeling alive, as harbour does.

clue.text: Put limits on a large urban area's size

parts.note: to cap is to set a maximum on
a city is a large town; the 's stands for 'has' as a link

explanation.surface: Planners restrict a sprawling city's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity is the amount something can hold, its volume or extent.

clue.text: Supportive type about to reform, in a way

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: the words are rearranged in a different way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A kindly person is on the point of changing their behaviour somewhat.
explanation.definitionFit: A comforter is someone who consoles and gives emotional support to people in distress.

clue.text: Cop summoning help, maybe, for artist

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who blows a whistle, as an old-time policeman did to call for help
second meaning: James McNeill ..., the American painter

explanation.walkthrough: Whistler was a 19th-century American-born painter famous for the portrait known as Whistler's Mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A whistler is anyone who whistles, such as a police officer calling for backup, and also the painter's surname.

clue.text: Insouciant participant in civil war

definitions.meaning: first meaning: offhand and carelessly unconcerned
second meaning: a Royalist supporter of Charles I in the English Civil War

explanation.walkthrough: The Cavaliers fought for the king against Cromwell's Roundheads in the 1640s.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is a dismissive, carefree one, and Cavaliers were the king's side in England's seventeenth-century conflict.

clue.text: In hearing, a means of controlling charge

indicators.note: in hearing means as it sounds when said, and also hints at a court hearing

parts.note: a rein, the strap for controlling a horse, said aloud

explanation.surface: In a court hearing, a method of restraint is used against the accused.
explanation.walkthrough: In hearing sounds like the court setting where an arraignment happens, but it is the signal that the pieces are spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a criminal accusation.

clue.text: Part of face — cheek or lip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the opening for eating and speaking

explanation.walkthrough: Cheek and lip both look like neighbouring parts of the face, but here they mean impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouth is a facial feature, and informally the word means backchat or impertinence.

clue.text: To release, remove ropes tied around European

indicators.note: the rope word is tied around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to unlash is to untie the lashings or ropes

explanation.surface: Someone frees a European bound with rope by undoing the knots.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to let something go free from restraint.

clue.text: Is a lawyer from US able to land across the border?

parts.note: can means be able to
DA is a district attorney, a US public prosecutor

explanation.surface: Asking whether an American lawyer is qualified to practise in a neighbouring country.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada lies across the northern frontier from the United States, so it is a neighbouring country.

clue.text: Moor, for example, moving around in a craft that's docked

indicators.note: moving around means the letters change places
a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A North African figure drifting about inside a boat with its stern cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's docked' trims CRAFT to CRAF; 'moving around' rearranges IN, A and CRAF. 'Moor' is not the moorland here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moors were Muslim people of North Africa, so a Moor is an example of someone from that continent.

clue.text: Animal arrived, then shortly left

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, arrived
L is the short form of left

explanation.surface: Someone turned up and then soon departed.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is a humped desert mammal used for riding and carrying loads.

clue.text: Name many stupid people

parts.note: oodles is informal for lots

explanation.surface: A crowd of fools, too numerous to name individually.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodle is informal slang for a silly person or a fool, so the plural means fools.

clue.text: Cricket side in an odd mood, initially, it's obvious

definitions.note: a noun phrase sense: something that is self-evident

indicators.note: the team piece sits in the middle of the initial letters
takes the first letter of each of the three words

parts.note: the first letter of each of these three words
a cricket team is an eleven, written in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cricket team in a strange mood plainly shows it from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a statement accepted as self-evident truth without needing proof.

clue.text: Person venerated like John and George, but not Ringo?

definitions.text: Person venerated like John and George, but not Ringo?

parts.words: Person venerated like John and George, but not Ringo?
parts.note: John and George are names of saints as well as Beatles; the remaining Beatle who is also a saint is the apostle, while there is no saint called Ringo

explanation.walkthrough: John, George and Ringo point to the Beatles; the fourth Beatle shares his name with the apostle, and Saint John and Saint George are also saints.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle and missionary to the Gentiles is honoured as a saint, sharing a first name with Paul McCartney.

clue.text: Record producer shrink listened to

indicators.note: as heard spoken, the psychiatrist word is pronounced the same as the answer

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist or analyst

explanation.surface: A music producer whose psychotherapist listens to his troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: Record producer suggests the music industry; it is a writer of annals.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist compiles annals, year-by-year historical records, so he produces records.

clue.text: Tell, for example, cunning ruler

parts.note: arch means sly or knowing
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A sly monarch's instruction to speak up.
explanation.walkthrough: Tell looks like a verb; it is William Tell, the Swiss folk hero who shot an apple from his son's head.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tell is the legendary Swiss marksman with a crossbow, an example of a bowman.
